sources.researchNote: The entry gives the theatre’s addresses: Nowy Świat 63 (5 September 1925 – 11 September 1926, hall of 1,000 seats), Marszałkowska 125 in the former Teatr Nowy (11 September 1926 – 28 August 1927) and Karowa 18 (30 August – 4 September 1927), and describes the dispute over the name that preceded the founding of Nowe Perskie Oko in November 1927 and of Morskie Oko.

media.title: Zula Pogorzelska in My chcemy króla at Teatr Perskie Oko (1926)
media.description: Stage photograph of Zula Pogorzelska in a scene from the revue “My chcemy króla” at Warsaw’s Teatr “Perskie Oko,” April 1926. The photograph provides visual context for the interwar revue environment in which Kaper’s earliest Warsaw songs and professional networks developed; it is not used as evidence for a Kaper credit in this revue.
media.altText: Black-and-white stage photograph of Zula Pogorzelska posing with a folding fan in an ornate costume and large decorative hat.
media.rightsNote: The linked source identifies this item as public domain or otherwise free of known copyright restrictions; attribution is retained.
media.publicCaption: Zula Pogorzelska in a scene from “My chcemy króla” at Teatr “Perskie Oko,” Warsaw, April 1926. The photograph documents the visual culture of the Warsaw revue stage during Kaper’s early professional period.

timelineEvents.title: Earliest published cabaret songs
timelineEvents.label: 1926 · Earliest published cabaret songs
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Kaper’s Warsaw cabaret songs appear in print under the pseudonym Bruno Asper, which the manuscripts show him already using in 1923.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Songs for Warsaw cabarets published under the pseudonym Bruno Asper, to words by Andrzej Włast. The printed editions of 1926 are the earliest published songs documented here; the signature itself is older, appearing on the 1923 manuscript of Koszutski Girls.

places.displayName: Teatr Perskie Oko, Nowy Świat 63, Warsaw
places.publicNote: Warsaw revue theatre founded by former members of Qui Pro Quo, where Zula Pogorzelska introduced Kaper’s first printed songs of 1926. Perskie Oko played at Nowy Świat 63 from 5 September 1925 to 11 September 1926, then at Marszałkowska 125 until August 1927. The coordinates give the modern address point of Nowy Świat 63; continuity with the pre-war building is not established.
